article.headline: Hiring for Taste: The Multimodal AI Research Role Takes Shape
article.lede: Nick St. Pierre — Creative Director, AI educator, and the voice behind the widely followed @nickfloats account — is not advertising for a prompt engineer. His announcement of an opening for people to "prompt all day" across image, video, music, and language models, with taste and tool obsession as the only requirements, points to something newer and more defensible: an artist-led research role in which the instrument is the prompt and the output is knowledge.
article.body:
St. Pierre is a creative director at OCA — an agency whose clients include Meta Platforms (META), Google (GOOGL), and Adobe (ADBE) — who has spent several years building what amounts to a public research practice around AI creative tools, teaching technique at Anderson Ranch Arts Center and to tens of thousands of practitioners through cohort-based courses online. The role he is advertising is an extension of that practice: not operations, not production, but systematic investigation of how image, video, music, and language models behave across inputs, parameters, and compositional styles.

The distinction matters because the category the announcement superficially resembles — *prompt engineering* — has spent two years being declared obsolete. Fortune reported in May 2025 that a role once advertised at up to $375,000 was "already obsolete thanks to AI." A Microsoft (MSFT) survey of 31,000 workers ranked it second-to-last among roles companies are considering adding. But that obituary applies to a specific version of the work: writing instructions to wring consistent outputs from text language models for business-process automation. Multimodal creative prompting — understanding why Runway's Gen-4 handles camera motion differently from Kuaishou Technology's (1024.HK) Kling, or how Suno's voice-cloning interacts with style prompting — is not something language models can yet do for themselves, and the knowledge is not codified anywhere.

The tools span four modalities whose simultaneous maturation defines the current moment. In image, **Midjourney** and Black Forest Labs' *FLUX* — founded in 2024, valued at $3.25 billion after a $300 million raise — contest photorealism and aesthetic range. In video, Runway and Google (GOOGL) Veo dominate creative-professional workflows; OpenAI's much-hyped *Sora* shut down entirely in April 2026. In music, Suno and Udio each settled copyright disputes with major labels in 2025 and are now positioned as collaborative rather than replacement tools. *Cross-modal fluency* — knowing how to compose a pipeline from image output through video, narration, and score — remains genuinely rare and underdocumented.

Companies are already paying for exactly this. ElevenLabs, the voice and audio AI firm, lists an "AI Creative Producer" role requiring deep expertise prompting image, video, and audio models — a description that might have been written by St. Pierre. Lightricks, maker of the LTX Studio video tool, advertises an "AI Creative Technologist" at $160,000 to $180,000 plus equity. Runway has arguably institutionalized the model through its Creative Partners Program, which treats working artists as a distributed feedback function inside product development. St. Pierre's announcement moves that logic from program to payroll.

Whether the role outlasts the current generation of models turns on what it actually produces. If the output is images, improving models will eventually outprompt any practitioner. If the output is documented frameworks, technique guides, and cross-modal workflow designs — the intellectual infrastructure that helps others work faster — that is research in the traditional sense, and better tools do not make the researcher redundant. A Semafor analysis of Gallup data published in May 2026 found that AI had not reduced artists' employment; artists were working slightly more hours than in 2022. The "artist-led research" framing is not semantic sleight of hand. It is the version of this job that might actually last.

concepts.definition: The practice of designing and refining text instructions — prompts — to elicit specific outputs from AI models. The term peaked as a job title in 2023 as companies sought specialists to optimize AI interactions; by 2025 it had largely collapsed, partly because models became capable enough that precise prompting mattered less for routine tasks, and partly because the skill was absorbed into broader technical and creative roles.

AI systems that process or generate more than one type of media — text, images, audio, and video — rather than being limited to a single data type. The latest generation of tools (2025–2026) can accept or produce combinations of modalities within a single workflow, enabling tasks like turning a text description into a video with synchronized music and narration.

The practical skill of composing workflows that move outputs from one AI modality into inputs for another — for example, generating an image, refining it into a video clip, writing narration, and scoring with AI-generated music. Each model has distinct aesthetic defaults and failure modes, and knowing how to chain them coherently is a competency not taught by any single tool's documentation.

A model for inquiry in which the research agenda is driven by aesthetic and creative questions rather than business-process or engineering goals. In the AI tools context, it means investigating model behavior, failure modes, and creative potential with a practitioner's sensibility — producing frameworks, technique guides, and workflow documentation as primary outputs rather than finished artworks.

ticker_meta.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
ticker_meta.blurb: Meta Platforms, headquartered in Menlo Park, California, operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads — collectively the largest social-media ecosystem in the world by monthly active users. The company generates the vast majority of its revenue through digital advertising, using detailed behavioural data to target ads across its platforms. After a painful 2022 in which shares fell roughly 65% amid a revenue slowdown and ballooning metaverse losses, Meta executed a dramatic turnaround by cutting costs, boosting margins, and rapidly integrating AI-driven ad ranking tools (Advantage+) that demonstrably improved advertiser returns. CEO Mark Zuckerberg declared 2023 a 'Year of Efficiency' and the company followed through. By late 2025 Meta was simultaneously the most profitable it had ever been and the most aggressive in AI infrastructure spending, committing up to $65 billion in capex for 2025 and raising that figure to as much as $145 billion for 2026.
ticker_meta.recent: Meta reached an all-time high near $796 per share in September 2025. The stock declined approximately 24–28% from that peak through April 2026, with the primary investor concern being the scale of the 2026 capital-expenditure commitment — up to $145 billion — and uncertainty about whether AI-driven revenue would materialise at the pace required to justify it. Quarterly earnings remained strong through the period, but multiple compression drove share-price weakness.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_adbe.name: Adobe Inc.
ticker_adbe.blurb: Adobe Inc. is a multinational software company known for its creative, marketing, and document management solutions, including Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat Reader, and the Experience Cloud. The company has transitioned to a subscription-based model, generating recurring revenue from its Digital Media and Digital Experience segments. Adobe holds a dominant position in the creative software market and competes with firms like Salesforce and Microsoft in the digital experience space.
ticker_adbe.recent: In the past 30 days, Adobe's stock has shown volatility amid broader tech market movements. The company reported strong quarterly earnings, beating analyst estimates on both revenue and earnings per share, driven by growth in its Digital Media segment. However, forward guidance was slightly below expectations, leading to mixed analyst reactions.

ticker_msft.name: Microsoft Corporation
ticker_msft.description: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.

ticker_1024-hk.name: Kuaishou Technology
ticker_1024-hk.blurb: Kuaishou Technology operates a leading short-video and live-streaming platform in China, known for its community-driven content and e-commerce integration. The company generates revenue through live-streaming gifts, advertising, and online shopping commissions. It competes with ByteDance's Douyin in the Chinese social media market.
ticker_1024-hk.recent: In the past 30 days, Kuaishou's stock has shown volatility with price swings of up to 7% in a single day. Analysts from Citi and UBS raised price targets to HKD95 and HKD108 respectively, reflecting optimism about the company's growth prospects. Block trades totaling millions of shares have been reported, indicating institutional activity.
